title: the bureau: xcom declassified
text: "Welcome back Commander." X-COM: Enemy Unknown (240 hours) is one of my favorite games to this date. It is one of the best turn based strategy games I have ever played. As XCOM EU is still a hit game, many will pan The Bureau: XCOM Declassified for not being on par with XCOM EU. I on the other hand believe that The Bureau is a fantastic game especially with that 75% deal from the Summer Sale (2014). Here is what the Bureau does good and bad in my opinion Pros: -Fun gameplay that is reminescent of the combat of Mass Effect 2/3. -Fair amount of time to complete everything (I played the game for a total of 23 hours when I wrote this review) -Characters are slightly better, there are only a few likeable characters. -The feel of the game is like Mass Effect but more realistic especially the movement during combat. Cons: -Story is great in the beginning but begins to suck by the end. -(Understand that the XCOM stories usually suck so cut 2K some slack) -The game could feel repetitive to some people. I never felt that it was repetitive. -24 hours of gameplay could be too short for some people. This game is $20 when not in sale and I believe that it could be a good buy to some but those tight on cash should wait till it's on sale for at least 50% off. VERDICT YES- You should get this game

title: the bureau: xcom declassified
text: If you enjoyed the combat systems in Mass Effect II or III or if you've enjoyed the Gears of War series, you'll enjoy the combat in The Bureau: XCOM Declassified. If you're a fan of the XCOM series you can appreciate it for that alone. Unlike previous XCOM titles, The Bureau is very story-driven. I'd go as far as to say that it plays just like a Mass Effect game set in the XCOM universe during the Cold War. You wander around the XCOM base talking to people and completing small sub-missions not unlike wandering around the Normandy in Mass Effect doing the same. Firaxis intends to tie the storyline of The Bureau in to the upcoming XCOM: Enemy Unknown expansion called The Enemy Within due out in November, so I'm eagerly anticipating the big things to come in the XCOM universe.

title: the bureau: xcom declassified
text: Okay, so before I say much I will just point out that I have not completed the game yet. I'm currently on a mission but got stuck due to a bug/glitch that makes parts of the map disappear. So, I'll restart the mission and move through it slower in order to hopefully have the map fully load. Anyways, for what it is - A tactical shoot 'em up with placement and semi-control of your AI companions, it's quite enjoyable. Personally I find the storyline to be quite enjoyable and cool. I also must say I love the voice acting. Some tedious legwork in the base MAY annoy some people, understandably, but hey it's not too bad. And sometimes the NPC's will say something as you walk by. Always cool to hear what people think of your character. In addition - You get to create four people right after the innitial mission however you want. The levelling system is intriguing as well and I find myself constantly thinking "Wow, I feel like I'm literally an agent/group of within the XCOM base." It's really a nice feeling when I was such a huge fan of "Enemy Unknown". Is the game fun, as a baseline qualifier? Yes! It is fun! Sure, it might not be what you're looking for in an XCOM game, but it's worth the buy and the play for those of you who like FPS games. And for those of you who enjoy retroesque storylines and stuff of the like, this could also find it's way to your heart as well. 8/10 - Though, if this bug persists my rating may change to a solid 7. If you read all of this, pat yourself on the back! Thanks for the read. And, for the creators of The Bureau: XCOM Declassified, thank you!

text: I remember this game getting a lot of "meh" reviews when it came out, but I think it deserved better.  The story isn't life-changing, but it is very interesting and different.  A huge amount of love clearly went into building the world and all the little stories within; the attention to detail should impress most who look.  Controlling the game, with it's heavy reliance on managing one's squad, is a little clunky and takes some getting used to.  However, you get to be good at it and feel pretty fancy when a plan goes like you want it to. Honestly, my biggest complaint is that Carter's voice is a parody of Modern Shooter Protagonist.  It's not Mark Hildreth's best work; he sounds like he's trying too hard to be gravelly.  Everyone else is good, though!  This game is definitely worth a play.  It's long enough to be a good value and fun enough that I didn't want to put it down for hours.

text: Hands down, my favourite survival game. The building system is amazing, and the fact that cannibals actually attack your base makes singleplayer so much more enjoyable than most other games. Part of what makes this so fun is that the AI provides a challenge, and you don't have to deal with crap like offline raiding which is the challenge in most games when building a base. Instead, you have plenty of time to set up a base, and then when it gets to a noticeable size, the cannibals will investigate and then bring the tribe to try and attack. The game is balanced, realistic and great fun. If you want a great game which you can enjoy in both singleplayer and multiplayer, then I definitely recommend this game. 9/10 Would dismember again

title: the forest
text: Now first of all. It's a great game and worth every cent. Maybe the best early access game I've ever played. Keep it going. The combination of survival in the wild and the constant threat of being eaten alive is amazing. The dark and hostile caves gave me one of the best experiences in gaming ever. Went into a cave, well equipped, about 30 minutes later I found myself lost and trapped, shaking, scared, poking in the dark with my spear, barely made it out alive with only a lighter and an axe. There should also be an evaluation of the player's sanity. That was maybe the most tense hour in my gaming life... Nevertheless I would like to give the devs some suggestions: - Survival in the wild is too easy. Only 4 days in my first game and I found myself so well equipped with meat, water and resources. There was no real challenge. Even when I set out to explore the island, I made it through 5 days without having any difficulty finding food or water. Deers would run around in front of me, just wating to be killed. So please: Make the hunting feel like real hunting! Let me track the blood of an injured animal. - A skill system would be nice. Not that I always need skill systems in games, but progress in this game should have a skill system. I mean, I'm some guy used to supermarkets, plastic wrapped meat, flat screens and netflix and I crash in the wild. Hunting should be a mess and very difficult at the beginning. After killing a couple of rabbits I might get better at this. - Please add more wildlife. I bet there's more to find on an island than lizards, rabbits, birds and deer. How about insects? - Animations are a little off. Especially for the spear and arrows when they hit an animal or enemy. would be nice to see them get stuck. Limb damage would be amazing - "Real" Dodging would be great - Why dont't I get bones from deers? - A greater variety of environments/maps would be awesome - Dead bodies should spread infections. Would be great to be able to dig a grave or burn bodies to keep myself from getting sick. - Sanity level doesn't really have an effect. Or at least I didn't feel it. I start to chop up humans and eat them for god sake. And that doesn't have any consequnece? - Using mud as camouflage. In general I would like some more "Lord of the flies" feeling - Bandages and more variety in medics, damage zones would be great Thanks for reading, whoever finds this useful. Great game and I'm really looking forward to the finished game! Keep up the good work!

title: the guild ii
text: As a long time strategy gamer, this looked like it was a perfect fit. The concept is great, but the execution is weak. Guild 2 had the potential to be something really amazing. Pros: The artwork on the towns and maps is well done despite the limitations of the graphics capabilities. The gameplay is innovative and provides a lot of varied options including building wealth by running your day to day business operations and expansion, getting involved in politics and the accompanying intrigue, sabotaging competitors, and building a family. Cons: The pathing AI is horrendous. Much of your time will be eaten away hoping that your toon can find their way home or to town hall. Speaking of time killers, as you get into politics, the meetings get longer and longer. They end up easily taking up half the game play time. So, it ends up being mandatory to set up AI control of your businesses. You will probably want to anyway after the first few interactions with managing your business on your own because it quickly goes from interesting to tedious. I put in almost 4 hours and desperately wanted to love the game. Also tried the Pirate expansion in the hopes it would fix some of the issues. Eventually it became too annoying to enjoy. This could have been something awesome with better design. But no.
